question: The famous Jain temple of Dilwara, built by Solanki rulers, is located at which place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mount Abu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dilwara Temples are a group of **Jain temples** located in **Mount Abu**, Rajasthan, India, renowned for their exquisite marble architecture and intricate craftsmanship.
 
• These temples were built between the **11th and 13th centuries** by the Solanki rulers and dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras (spiritual teachers).
 
• There are five prominent temples at Dilwara: **Vimal Vasahi, Luna Vasahi, Pittalhar, Parshvanatha, and Mahavir Swami**, each known for its unique architectural beauty.
 
• The **Vimal Vasahi Temple**, dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankara, Adinath, is the oldest and most elaborate, constructed in 1031 AD by Vimal Shah, a minister of the Solanki dynasty.
 
• The temples are particularly famous for their **intricate marble carvings**, including ceilings, pillars, and doorways, showcasing unparalleled artistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mount Abu** is a popular hill station in Rajasthan and the only one in the state, located in the Aravalli Range. It is known for its scenic beauty and historical significance.
 
• The **Solanki dynasty**, also known as the Chaulukya dynasty, was a prominent ruling dynasty in Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan during the medieval period, known for their patronage of art and architecture.
 
• Jainism is an ancient Indian religion known for its emphasis on **non-violence (Ahimsa)**, asceticism, and the pursuit of spiritual liberation through self-discipline and meditation.
 
• The Dilwara temples serve as an important pilgrimage site for Jains and are also admired by art enthusiasts and historians for their architectural brilliance.
 
• Mount Abu is also home to other attractions like the **Nakki Lake** and the **Achalgarh Fort**, making it a significant tourist destination.
